Is it possible to provide a complexity analysis of the algorithm? The description of how the DeepONet architecture is used to solve the coupled PDEs and compute the loss is insufficient. The core idea revolves around leveraging the dynamic formulation of the optimal transport (OT) problem, which is characterized by a system of coupled partial differential equations (PDEs) in both primal and dual spaces. Instead of directly solving these PDEs for each new pair of distributions, GeONet learns a neural operator that approximates the solution, effectively mapping pairs of initial and terminal distributions to their corresponding geodesic path. This is achieved by training a neural network, specifically a modified DeepONet architecture, to minimize a loss function that enforces the optimality conditions derived from the Benamou-Brenier formulation of OT. The loss function incorporates terms that penalize deviations from the continuity equation, the Hamilton-Jacobi equation, and the boundary conditions. The authors demonstrate the effectiveness of GeONet through a series of experiments, primarily focusing on Gaussian mixture distributions in 1D and 2D settings. They compare the performance of GeONet against traditional OT solvers from the POT library, as well as other learning-based methods like Conditional Flow Matching (CFM) and Rectified Flow (RF) on point cloud data. The results indicate that GeONet achieves significant speedups compared to traditional solvers while maintaining reasonable accuracy. The paper also explores the application of GeONet to the MNIST dataset, using a latent space representation of the digits. However, the results on MNIST are less compelling, highlighting the challenges of applying the method to complex, real-world data. Overall, the paper presents an interesting and promising approach to learning Wasserstein geodesics using neural operators, offering a potentially more efficient alternative to traditional numerical solvers. However, the lack of theoretical analysis and the limited evaluation on high-dimensional and complex datasets raise questions about the generalizability and robustness of the proposed method.

The use of a modified DeepONet architecture is also a positive aspect, as it provides a flexible framework for approximating the solution operators of the coupled PDE system.
